headlines.title: Chip stocks fall as equipment maker Lam Research cites 'supply chain constraints'
headlines.summary: Chip stocks declined on Thursday amid concerns about supply constraints and lingering worries about the AI trade.

headlines.title: Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA Corporation, FormFactor, and Penguin Solutions shares plummet, what you need to know
headlines.summary: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after warnings emerged that ongoing component supply chain bottlenecks and cleanroom space constraints will restrict semiconductor equipment makers from meeting demand through 2027.

headlines.title: Applied Materials Sinks 7% on Lam’s Outlook: “A Bit Higher” Wasn’t Enough
headlines.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT:NASDAQ) shares are down about 7. 4% today (trading at about $380) after Lam Research (LRCX:NASDAQ) said supply-chain constraints held back its December-quarter outlook.

headlines.title: Lam Research Sinks 9% as Supply Constraints Cap Outlook; Applied Materials Drops 6%, ASML Holding Falls 4%
headlines.summary: A record quarter wasn't enough to keep chip equipment stocks out of the red after Lam Research's CFO let slip a phrase that spooked the entire semiconductor sector and sent shares tumbling hard.

headlines.title: Can Semiconductor Systems Drive AMAT's Next Growth Phase?
headlines.summary: Applied Materials is capitalizing on AI chip demand as advanced logic, DRAM and packaging investments fuel Semiconductor Systems growth and margin expansion.

description: Applied Materials, Inc. provides materials engineering solutions, equipment, services, and software to the semiconductor and related industries in the United States, China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through Semiconductor Systems and Applied Global Services (AGS) segments. The Semiconductor Systems segment includes semiconductor capital equipment to enable materials engineering steps, including etch, rapid thermal processing, deposition, chemical mechanical planarization, metrology and inspection, wafer packaging, and ion implantation. The AGS segment offers integrated solutions to optimize equipment and fab performance and productivity comprising spares, upgrades, services, and 200 millimeter and other equipment and factory automation software for semiconductor and other products. It serves manufacturers of semiconductor wafers and chips, and other electronic devices. Applied Materials, Inc. was incorporated in 1967 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
